title: Streamline legacy networking overlays and orchestrate AWS provider migration with incremental-plan driver
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: We have accumulated significant planning latency and brittle networking overlays across our Terraform stacks. This ticket aims to: 1) simplify the networking template surface by extracting a minimal base network module and thin environment overlays, 2) introduce an "incremental-plan" orchestration driver to run targeted downstream plans instead of full-matrix plans (reduce CI run time), and 3) migrate the AWS provider pin from ~>3.x to the v5.x compatible constraint across infra repos while preserving safe rollbacks and state integrity. Deliverables: refactored base_network module, overlay thin layer, new CI job (tf-incremental-plan), provider constraint updates + module compat shims, documented state migration steps and rollback playbook.
acceptance_criteria: base_network module implements VPC/subnet/route/nat with stable inputs and output contracts
overlay modules reference base_network via explicit module inputs and remove inlined region logic
CI incremental-plan reduces median plan time across networking changes by >=40% on staging
AWS provider bumped to ">=5.0.0, <6.0.0" in infra mono-repo and companion repos with no plan drift in staging
State migration executed for two pilot workspaces (staging-us-east-1, staging-eu-west-1) with verified resource counts and automated rollback snapshot
Runbook and automated validation scripts committed under infra/docs/provider-migration/ with approvals from Security and SRE

Design base_network module API and backward-compat shim (owner: Miguel) - PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1823
Implement incremental-plan CI job: terraform graph + targeted apply plan driver (owner: Jordan Lee) - CI branch: ci/incremental-plan
Introduce provider-compat shims in modules where aws provider aliasing or resource names changed (owner: Devops eng) - patch PRs per repo
Pilot provider bump in staging workspaces and run full drift verification (owner: Miguel) - workspace: staging-us-east-1
Create state snapshot and automated rollback steps using remote backend snapshot tooling (owner: SRE lead)
Run canary apply for a single non-prod account, run perf and connectivity tests, collect telemetry and cost signals
Rollout provider bump to remaining non-prod workspaces, then production following the rollout matrix in the runbook
Post-migration: prune legacy overlay modules and add deprecation warnings for 30 days
notes: 2026-03-01: Ticket created after infra SIG review; priority raised due to repeated CI regressions and long plan times impacting delivery.

2026-03-03: Initial audit complete. Found 17 overlays that inline region selection and 5 places with manual aws provider aliasing. Large contributors to plan churn: conditional resource count and dynamic for_each with non-deterministic keys.
2026-03-05: Spike results: extracting a base module reduced plan delta by ~30% on a toy environment. Incremental-plan proof-of-concept reduced CI job time from 14m to 6m for targeted changes.

2026-03-07: Security review requested for provider bump (KMS/HSM integrations touched). Security flagged provider credential behavior change; added a validation step to CI to assert cross-account role ARNs remain unchanged.

2026-03-09: Created PR in infra mono-repo to add provider constraint and compatibility shim (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1823). Waiting on automated test matrix (plan-only) and SRE approval for pilot workspace run.

2026-03-10: Began pilot workspace migration in staging-us-east-1. Snapshot taken before state mv. No drift observed after provider change in first pilot; continuing rollout to staging-eu-west-1 next week.

Merge provider constraint PR gated behind plan-only approvals
